mainEntity.name: What does it mean to digitize yacht maintenance records properly?

acceptedAnswer.text: It means three things: the records have to be text you can search rather than pictures of text, they have to be connected to the equipment, faults and work orders they relate to, and they have to be retrievable by a plain-language question rather than by knowing the filing convention. A drive of image-only scans meets none of these.

mainEntity.name: Do I have to re-type or reformat everything to make it searchable?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and trying to is what stalls most projects. Existing manuals, PDFs, scans, exports and emails should be indexed in their current formats. Scanning paper through text recognition adds a searchable layer without discarding the originals. The reformatting exercise is the step to avoid, not the step to start with.

mainEntity.name: Can I bring my existing records with me?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. CelesteOS is the planned maintenance system, and your existing manuals, PDFs, scans, and exports are imported as they are, with no reformatting. The pilot includes importing the equipment register, certificates, and work-order history, so the vessel's full history is findable in one place.

mainEntity.name: Why isn't a folder of scanned PDFs enough?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because a scan is a picture of text. You can only find a file in that folder if you already know its name or where it sits, which is precisely the knowledge that leaves with the engineer who filed it. Digitizing properly means the contents are searchable, the records are connected to each other, and a plain question returns the source record rather than a snippet.
